Senator Rand Paul alleges scientific cover-up and calls for new research oversight legislation
J. I. Wood
Senator Rand Paul, chair of the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and an ophthalmologist from Kentucky, made a series of posts on July 22, 2026, alleging scientific misconduct related to the COVID-19 pandemic and calling for legislative action.
In his first post at 12:43 UTC, Paul wrote: "The cover-up is not a question. It is only a question of how pervasive. The Slack messages reveal that these scientists planned to “stay off of email” & “carefully curate some emails for FOI records.” They admit to deleting the paper trail that leads to the truth."
At 13:04 UTC on the same day, he followed up with another statement targeting Dr. Anthony Fauci, "Fauci’s lies and deception contributed to the deaths of 15 million Americans and countless loved ones worldwide. My Risky Research Review Act will ensure no rogue scientist can ever repeat these deadly mistakes."
Later that morning at 13:31 UTC, Paul shared resources for further information by posting: "All the documents: https://t.co/eI6z9DW6Xd https://t.co/EsaBHbnAWR"
Paul has been active in both politics and medicine. He performs pro-bono eye surgeries for patients in Kentucky and abroad, according to his official website. Paul earned his medical degree from Duke University School of Medicine and founded the Southern Kentucky Lions Eye Clinic. He also assists Kentucky residents with federal government agency matters.
The allegations against Dr. Fauci referenced in Paul's tweets are part of ongoing debates about pandemic response oversight in Congress.
